subject: Stability synthesis & QBR packet — action items for exec summary
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Stability synthesis & QBR packet — action items for exec summary

Team,

Following up on last week's BrightCart incident (SUP-9876). Attached is the current postmortem draft and the SLA impact spreadsheet — both are work-in-progress but complete enough for QBR prep. Quick synthesis up front:

- Impact: 27 min of degraded request routing on our US-west serving pool during peak (14:03–14:30 PDT 2026-08-10). Token-generation latency > 2s for ~18% of requests, which triggered BrightCart's SLO alerting and multiple production errors for their checkout microflow.
- Root cause (summary): underprovisioned autoscaler reaction to a sudden client-side traffic fanout plus a kernel scheduling regression in v1.3.2 serving runtime.
- Customer surface: BrightCart reported higher error rates and a spike in support tickets; they asked for a formal SLA classification and commercial remediation.

As we prepare slides for the QBR (Aug 24), I need the following from owners by COB Aug 20: 
1) A one-paragraph incident narrative for slide deck (owner: Marissa) — 2–3 sentences focused on what happened + current status.
2) Action-item roster with owners and target dates (owner: me) — compiled into the attached sheet.
3) A recommended commercial remediation (credit %, precedent, and legal notes) for the exec table (owner: Vivek + Neha).
4) A one-line ops mitigation summary we can show to BrightCart (owner: Evelyn).

Please see inline notes in the postmortem-draft.pdf. I flagged the highest-priority mitigations: autoscaler tuning, hot-path kernel revert/patch, and a short-term deployment guard. I've also put a tentative customer communication draft in the Drive link.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf, sla-impact-spreadsheet.xlsx

Thanks — happy to take quick syncs if helpful.

—
David Kim
Head of Reliability Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stability synthesis & QBR packet — action items for exec summary

David — thanks for the clear callouts. A few clarifications from SRE + runtime: 

- Timeline tweak: the autoscaler feed lag started at 14:00 PDT and metrics only crossed the responsive threshold at ~14:07; degraded routing plateaued until 14:28. I'm updating the timeline in the draft (see postmortem v1.1).
- Mitigations: ops completed a safe autoscaler config rollback on 8/11 and a staged kernel queue cap at 8/12; these reduced error rates by ~85% for affected requests. Permanent kernel fix ETA: patch submission by 8/21, bake/validation 8/22–8/23.

For the QBR slide asks: I can write the one-paragraph narrative (I'll keep it customer-facing and non-technical) and produce a two-line remediation summary for BrightCart. I propose we mark action "patch + validation" as highest priority (owner: runtime eng lead) and autoscaler policy as high (owner: SRE lead).

Open question: do we classify this as an SLA breach for BrightCart under our standard credit table? My read is yes — uptime degraded and error-rate SLO crossed the threshold; final call to finance/legal on credit percentage.

I'll attach a short timeline snippet to the postmortem and push v1.1 later today.

—
Marissa Cole
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks — good compendium. A few executive points: 

1) Customer commercial: I'm okay with offering a one-time credit up to 7% of the monthly invoice as a starting point, pending Neha + Finance confirmation and Legal sign-off. If BrightCart pushes back, we'll escalate to a 10% cap on a case-by-case basis. Neha, please run the numbers and loop Finance.

2) Messaging: keep the external communication focused on impact + steps we've taken (no kernel-level specifics). Marissa, your one-paragraph should read as: 1) what happened at a high level, 2) immediate mitigations we executed, 3) the next steps and ownership.

3) QBR deliverable: I need a single-slide executive summary (one-paragraph + 3 bullets for action items) and a backup slide with the SLA impact table. David — collect the final action roster and hand both to me by EOD Aug 20 so I can review before QBR prep sync on Aug 21.

4) Legal: defer the credit wording to Legal for the templated contract amendment. CC Legal on the proposed credit and request a fast-track review.

I'll join a quick 15m standup if useful tomorrow.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
COO
Redwood Inference
